definitions.explanation: Going out to buy something or deliver something on behalf of someone else. Commonly used when a parent sends a child to the store, or when someone runs errands for the household.

examples.japanese: お{使|つか}いに{行|い}ってきて。
examples.english: Go run an errand for me.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{初|はじ}めてのお{使|つか}いに{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: The child went out on their first errand.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}に{頼|たの}まれて、スーパーにお{使|つか}いに{行|い}った。
examples.english: My mother asked me to go on an errand to the supermarket.

notes:
The お prefix is standard and nearly always used; the bare form {使|つか}い sounds blunt and is rarely heard.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- お{使|つか}いに{行|い}く: to go on an errand
- お{使|つか}いを{頼|たの}む: to ask someone to run an errand
- お{使|つか}いに{出|で}かける: to go out on an errand

CULTURAL NOTE:
'{初|はじ}めてのお{使|つか}い' (My First Errand) is a popular Japanese TV show where small children are sent on errands alone for the first time, watched by hidden cameras. The concept reflects the cultural practice of gradually giving children independence through errands.

USAGE:
Most commonly associated with children being sent to buy something at a nearby store. For adult errands in a business context, {用事|ようじ} (business, things to do) is more natural.
